name: Additional business goals

selectedAnswers.prompt: Can a new potential customer understand what you sell within a few seconds of hearing or reading your explanation?

selected.text: Yes. I can explain our primary offer clearly in one simple sentence.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Does your primary offer promise a clear outcome or improvement for the customer?

selected.text: Yes. The desired customer outcome is specific and central to the offer.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How clearly defined is the customer your primary offer is intended for?

selected.text: Extremely clear. We know who benefits most and who generally isn’t a good fit.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How frequently do qualified prospects question the value, price, or reason they should choose your offer?

selected.text: Rarely. Qualified prospects generally understand why the offer is valuable.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How much evidence do you have that people actually want this offer?

selected.text: Strong evidence. We consistently sell it and/or customers repeatedly seek it out.

selectedAnswers.prompt: If qualified traffic to your offer doubled tomorrow, how confident would you feel sending those people into the current sales experience?

selected.text: Very confident. More qualified traffic would be welcome.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How clearly can you identify the type of customer who gets the most value from your primary offer?

selected.text: Very clearly. Our best customers share identifiable characteristics, problems, circumstances, or goals.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Do your best customers tend to share a specific problem, trigger, or situation that causes them to start looking for a solution like yours?

selected.text: Yes. We understand the specific situations or problems that typically create demand.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How often are the leads or prospects reaching you actually a good fit for what you sell?

selected.text: Most are reasonably well qualified.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How well do you understand what your customer is ultimately trying to accomplish beyond simply buying your product or service?

selected.text: Very well. We understand the larger business, professional, practical, or personal outcome they want.

selectedAnswers.prompt: If you needed to put your offer in front of 1,000 ideal prospects, do you know who those people would be and where you could realistically reach them?

selected.text: Yes. We know who they are and have several realistic ways to reach them.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Can a new visitor understand the main value you provide within the first few seconds of seeing your website, landing page, ad, or profile?

selected.text: Yes. The main outcome and value are immediately clear.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Does your marketing emphasize what changes for the customer, or mostly describe what you provide?

selected.text: We strongly emphasize customer outcomes and transformation.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How closely does your marketing language reflect the actual problems, goals, and words your customers use?

selected.text: Very closely. Our messaging is informed by sales conversations, reviews, research, search behavior, or other direct evidence.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Can a potential customer quickly understand why they should choose you instead of another reasonable alternative?

selected.text: Yes. Our differentiation is clear, relevant, and meaningful to the customer.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Does your marketing create a meaningful emotional reason for the customer to care?

selected.text: Yes. Our messaging connects clearly to meaningful ambitions, frustrations, fears, desires, identity, or relief.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How much credible evidence supports the important claims you make in your marketing?

selected.text: A lot. We regularly use relevant testimonials, reviews, results, case studies, demonstrations, data, associations, or other proof.

selectedAnswers.prompt: When someone reaches your main conversion page or experience, is the primary action you want them to take immediately clear?

selected.text: Yes. There is one obvious primary action.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How much work does a visitor have to do before they understand why taking the next step is worthwhile?

selected.text: Very little. The value and next step are clear near the beginning.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How well does the promise that gets someone to your website or landing page match what they encounter once they arrive?

selected.text: Very closely. The promise, language, offer, and next step feel consistent.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How much unnecessary friction exists between interest and conversion?

selected.text: Very little. The process is simple and intentional.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How strong is the proof or reassurance around the point where you’re asking someone to take action?

selected.text: Strong. Relevant proof and reassurance are located close to the decision.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How well does your conversion experience match the level of commitment you’re asking from the visitor?

selected.text: Very well. The amount of information, proof, and friction fits the decision.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Do you know which traffic sources primarily introduce new people to your business versus bringing back people who already know you?

selected.text: Yes. We clearly understand which channels play prospecting, retargeting, branded, referral, organic, or similar roles.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Do you know whether enough new demand is entering the system to support the conversions and growth you want?

selected.text: Yes. We understand how much new traffic or lead volume enters the funnel and approximately what happens afterward.

selectedAnswers.prompt: When performance changes, how confidently can you determine whether the cause is traffic, the offer, the website, product or merchandising changes, pricing, tracking, follow-up, or something else?

selected.text: Very confidently. We have enough data and process to investigate across the customer journey.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Are your acquisition channels intentionally assigned different roles, or are you expecting every channel to do everything?

selected.text: Yes. Different channels have clear strategic roles.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Do you have someone with dedicated responsibility and time to keep improving your paid advertising through testing?

selected.text: Yes. Someone has clear responsibility and protected time, runs a prioritized testing program, and regularly applies what we learn.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Do you know what you can afford to pay for a customer and a qualified lead—and the target that makes advertising worthwhile?

selected.text: Yes. We calculate and regularly review affordable customer and qualified-lead costs using close rates, customer value, costs, and margins.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Do you review both the return from individual advertising platforms and the overall return from your advertising investment?

selected.text: Yes. We regularly review both and use them together to guide budget and growth decisions.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How clearly can you explain those results and what they mean for the business?

selected.text: We review changes alongside spend, customer volume, customer quality, and profitability, and can explain our decisions.

selectedAnswers.prompt: How consistently do you develop and test new advertising ideas to find your next opportunity?

selected.text: We have an ongoing pipeline of ideas informed by customers and performance, and use each round of testing to improve the next.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Are your campaigns optimizing for the results that create real value for your business?

selected.text: Yes. We verify that the outcomes and values used for optimization reflect valuable purchases or qualified opportunities, or the intended role of awareness campaigns.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Have you clearly defined the small number of business outcomes that matter most for judging whether marketing is working?

selected.text: Yes. We have a small, clearly defined set of primary business KPIs.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Do you distinguish between outcome KPIs and diagnostic KPIs?

selected.text: Yes. We intentionally use both and understand their different purposes.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Do you maintain a KPI report or dashboard that lets you compare the same important metrics over time?

selected.text: Yes. It is consistently updated and actively used for decisions.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Does your team agree on where important KPIs come from, which sources should be treated as authoritative, and whether the data is reliable enough to make decisions?

selected.text: Yes. We have clear sources of truth and regularly validate important tracking.

selectedAnswers.prompt: Can you connect marketing activity to meaningful downstream business outcomes?

selected.text: Yes. We can connect acquisition to meaningful downstream outcomes.

selectedAnswers.prompt: When performance changes, do you have a consistent process for reviewing the data, recent changes, and customer journey before making major marketing decisions?

selected.text: Yes. We review business outcomes, diagnostic KPIs, tracking, recent changes, and the broader funnel before acting.

report.introduction: Your selected goals are trials or demos, registrations, store visits, subscribers, another business outcome. Your answers point to direct evidence of demand, a useful understanding of your best-fit customers, and a clear next step. Those are useful foundations to keep. No specific weakness is identified. For your lead-generation business, the next opportunity is to validate the quality of opportunities behind reported lead results. The three moves will check a recent evidence sample, define one useful testable idea and complete a small, clearly defined validation exercise or an explicit no-change decision.
report.trendNote: You reported advertising returns as “Generally stable”. This is context, not a score or proof of a cause. Check spend, volume, customer quality, margins, seasonality, and conversion delays before interpreting it; improving returns can coexist with shrinking total profit, and declining returns can accompany deliberate expansion.

recommendations.why: The next learning question should fit your business outcome and the process you already report as effective.

recommendations.title: Check the idea while keeping current activity stable
recommendations.whatToDo: Use the existing advertising owner and testing process you report as effective. Prepare or run the small, clearly defined validation exercise only within the confirmed resources, keeping successful activity stable; record a no-change decision if no useful testable idea is supported. Review the selected business goals separately; one goal’s volume or cost target does not establish success for another.

thirtyDayPlan.title: Establish the evidence
thirtyDayPlan.objective: Understand the quality of opportunities behind reported lead results before making changes.
actions: Trace a feasible sample of qualified opportunities to sales and customer value, allowing for close rates and sales delays.
Record observed facts, assumptions and missing information.
Record a separate baseline and useful measure for each selected business goal.
thirtyDayPlan.completionCriteria: A relevant baseline and its limits are documented before the decision.

thirtyDayPlan.title: Choose the improvement
thirtyDayPlan.objective: Choose a response the evidence and available resources can support.
actions: Choose one customer-quality or message testable idea that the existing process can evaluate; define the useful customer action and follow-up period.
thirtyDayPlan.completionCriteria: A small, clearly defined decision records its evidence, owner, resources, success/review criteria and any reason to defer.

thirtyDayPlan.title: Complete the agreed work
thirtyDayPlan.objective: Carry out the agreed improvement, validation or readiness work; a live campaign or website change is not required.
actions: Use the existing advertising owner and testing process you report as effective. Prepare or run the small, clearly defined validation exercise only within the confirmed resources, keeping successful activity stable; record a no-change decision if no useful testable idea is supported.
thirtyDayPlan.completionCriteria: A recent evidence sample documents the quality of opportunities behind reported lead results, including limitations. A testable idea names the business outcome, comparison, owner, limits and review period. A small, clearly defined validation exercise or an evidence-supported no-change decision is documented with an owner, comparison, limits and review date.

thirtyDayPlan.title: Evaluate the completed work
thirtyDayPlan.objective: Review the work already completed and what you learned before deciding what comes next.
actions: Review qualified opportunity volume, close rates, customer value, resource use and uncertainty; allow more time if sales have not matured.
Compare the completed work with the agreed completion criteria. Record the result, limitations and a keep, refine, defer or stop decision; any further implementation belongs in a later plan.
Evaluate each selected business goal against its own baseline; record tradeoffs rather than combining unlike results.
thirtyDayPlan.completionCriteria: A review note evaluates the completed work and records a decision without claiming unsupported performance gains.
